1918.title: internal error when use omp Agent
1918.rootCauseOneLine: plugins/provider-acp/src/bridge/bridge.ts resolveBridgeProcessArgsForMcpServer() uses process.argv[1] as the bb-bridge MCP server entry, but since #1640 (0.39.0) argv[1] is the provider-bridge bootstrap (bb-provider-bridge-worker.mjs / bridge-worker-entry.ts), so the MCP child exits 1 with a usage error and omp rejects session/new with "bb-bridge: Transport closed" (surfaced only as "Internal error" because agent-connection.ts drops error.data).
1918.proposedFix: In plugins/provider-acp/src/bridge/bridge.ts replace resolveBridgeProcessArgsForMcpServer() body with `return [...process.execArgv, fileURLToPath(import.meta.url), "--mcp-stdio"];` (the bridge's own module URL is the artifact in every launch mode; argv[1] is always the bootstrap now). Verified: repro test fails on d81fee6f and passes with the change, full provider-acp suite (162 tests) and typecheck pass, and an acp-omp thread on the dev instance gets past thread/start. No wire change, so no HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump. Keep a test that actually executes the advertised MCP command (the existing tests only hit the TCP side channel). Separately, agent-connection.ts:141-147 should append error.data.details to the rejected Error so agent-side failures are diagnosable from UI/daemon logs.
1918.caveats: omp is not installed on this machine; I installed @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent@17.3.8 plus bun 1.3.14 under /tmp for the repro (issue used 17.3.7 on macOS/Electron; my repro is Linux from source, where argv[1] is bridge-worker-entry.ts instead of bb-provider-bridge-worker.mjs — same mechanism). With the fix applied, the omp turn still fails with "Internal error" in my sandbox because omp has no model credentials ("No model selected"), so I could not verify a full successful omp turn. cursor-agent and grok tolerate the dead MCP server (session/new OK), so for those providers the bug manifests only as a silently missing update_environment_directory tool, which I did not exercise. The issue's "first session sometimes succeeds" claim is unverified (deterministic failure in all my runs). Worktree left with the fix applied and the repro test added (uncommitted). ~/.omp was created by my dev-instance run and removed at cleanup.

1919.title: storage.database() opens a new SQLite handle on every call; plugins leak fds until dispose
1919.rootCauseOneLine: apps/server/src/services/plugins/plugin-api.ts storage.database() does `new Database(...)` on every call and only pushes to databaseHandles (drained solely on dispose/reload), so each call holds fds on data.db/data.db-wal forever, unlike the SDK contract and the fake host which return one cached handle.
1919.proposedFix: In createPluginApi (plugin-api.ts ~L597) keep a `let databaseHandle: Database.Database | undefined`; in database() return it when `databaseHandle?.open`, otherwise open a new one, assign it, and still push onto databaseHandles so existing dispose/reload/rollback close paths are unchanged. Verified: repro test goes from failing (200 distinct handles / 200 fds) to passing, full apps/server plugins suite (381 tests) passes, typecheck passes, live server shows 1 fd after 300 calls instead of 301. Also tighten the backend-contract.ts comment to say the same handle is returned for the plugin load's lifetime. No protocol version bump needed.
1919.caveats: The issue's specific numbers (42,498 fds, spawn EBADF on the Factory install) were not re-measured since the Factory plugin was not available; the mechanism and unbounded growth are verified with a synthetic chatty plugin and a unit test. The fd-count assertion in the repro test uses /proc/self/fd (Linux only); the distinct-handle assertion is portable. The worktree contains the uncommitted proposed fix plus the new test file (not pushed).

1873.title: Uncaught C++ exception from PtyFork crashes the whole app (SIGABRT, no JS error frame)
1873.rootCauseOneLine: The daemon bundle statically imports @parcel/watcher (esbuild hoists host-watcher's "lazy" import of an internal module), so watcher.node (NAPI_DISABLE_CPP_EXCEPTIONS) loads before pty.node (NAPI_CPP_EXCEPTIONS) in one process; on macOS dyld coalesces the identical weak Napi::details::CallbackData<...>::Wrapper symbol to watcher.node's try/catch-less copy, so when PtyFork throws Napi::Error on a failed spawn nothing catches it and the daemon aborts.
1873.proposedFix: In packages/host-watcher/src/parcel-watcher-backend.ts make the in-process fallback do `const { default: parcelWatcher } = await import("@parcel/watcher")` (dynamic import of the external package stays lazy in the esbuild ESM bundle) instead of importing the internal real-parcel-watcher.js wrapper; re-verified in this pass that the repro vitest fails on d81fee6f and passes with the diff, and the rebuilt daemon bundle loads only pty.node. Guard with a test asserting the bundle has no static top-level import of @parcel/watcher. Optionally load node-pty first as defense in depth, and upstream a node-pty fix (try/catch in native entry points or -fvisibility=hidden/GCC_SYMBOLS_PRIVATE_EXTERN in binding.gyp).
1873.caveats: Revision addressed all verifier findings: (major) napi-wrapper-coalesce-linux.cjs now resolves the platform addon via createRequire(require.resolve("@parcel/watcher")) and its usage comment says SIGSEGV-on-Linux/SIGABRT-on-macOS; both linux-rtld-*.log files, daemon-bundle-addon-load-order*.log and macho-weak-syms-output.log were regenerated in a fresh worktree at d81fee6f with NODE_PATH unset (paths shown as <repo>); (minor) macho-weak-syms.py now skips N_STAB debug entries and prints addr=, and the report explains the earlier ext=False lines. Added run-*.sh helper scripts under repro/ and a Verification subsection at the end of the report. Still no macOS host, so the SIGABRT itself was not re-run; the macOS leg rests on Mach-O analysis of the shipped darwin-arm64 prebuilts, the reporter's stack, and the Linux RTLD_GLOBAL analog. The specific errno on the reporter's machine is unverified. Worktree wf_d5c47f31-487-11 is at d81fee6f (detached) with the prototype fix and repro test uncommitted; no dev instance was started, ports 12707/20707/28707 confirmed free, data dir absent.

1915.title: Incompatible plugins unload silently — no error, warning, log line, or startup surface across a minor upgrade
1915.rootCauseOneLine: loadOne()'s pre-factory failure branch (failBeforeFactory in apps/server/src/services/plugins/plugin-runtime.ts) only calls setStatus() and returns, so an engines.bb mismatch sets status=incompatible in memory without any logger line (unlike the 'plugin X loaded' / 'failed to load' siblings), and no app/CLI surface aggregates or volunteers that status.
1915.proposedFix: Server: add logger.warn in failBeforeFactory (and the hungServices 'degraded' branch) in plugin-runtime.ts so every non-running load outcome is logged like 'plugin <id> not loaded (incompatible): requires bb >=0.38.0 <0.39.0, this is 0.39.0' (two-line prototype in 1915/repro/proposed-fix.diff makes the repro test pass); optionally one aggregate summary line after loadAll(). App: surface an aggregate needs-attention count (incompatible/error/missing) on the Extensions nav or a dismissible banner, reusing the existing plugins.list() status/statusDetail; show statusDetail in the detail banner. CLI: include non-running plugins in `bb status` (or a `bb plugin doctor`). No protocol version bump needed.
1915.caveats: Host version was simulated with BB_APP_VERSION on a dev instance (dev builds default to 0.0.0 which skips the engines gate entirely, so this path is invisible in normal dev). The reporter's third-party plugins (Notify/agent-proxy) were not available; a fixture plugin with the same engines range was used. The 'external process stays alive while the plugin binding is gone' claim is plugin-specific and was not verified. Worktree left with one untracked file (the repro test); prototype fix was reverted.

1914.title: A rate-limited workflow call reports only 'Workflow worker failed' — the 429 is hidden in a child thread
1914.rootCauseOneLine: Server builds the plugin `thread.failed` payload's `error` from `system/error` rows only (apps/server/src/services/threads/thread-data.ts getLastThreadErrorMessage → db getLatestThreadSystemErrorEventRow); provider-originated failures (Claude 429) are persisted as provider/error + turn/completed failed with no system/error, so plugins get error:null and the workflows plugin falls back to "Workflow worker failed" (also killing its rate-limit retry classifier and giving automations "Turn failed").
1914.proposedFix: Fix at the server boundary: add a db query returning the latest failure row across system/error AND provider/error (scoped to events since the last root turn/started to avoid stale willRetry errors), make getLastThreadErrorMessage format provider/error as `detail ?? message (category, HTTP nnn, providerCode)`, and optionally add a structured experimental_ errorInfo/resetsAt field to the thread.failed payload (update backend-contract doc + docs/api_to_audit.md; no HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump needed). Then have the workflows plugin use the category to skip the 1s/4s retries for blocked subscription-window 429s and print "rate limited (429), resets HH:MM". A prototype patch (/tmp/bb-reports/issues/1914/repro/prototype-fix.patch) makes the server repro pass, keeps plugin-thread-events.test.ts green (12/12) and typechecks @bb/server.
1914.caveats: Worktree HEAD was 0f6759a74 (base d81fee6f + 2 unrelated commits #1912/#1923); neither touches the affected paths. Live 429 was produced with a fake Anthropic endpoint (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL) rather than a genuinely exhausted account, but it yields the identical claude-code rate_limit_event/provider/error/turn-completed-failed event sequence as the issue's thread. The reporter's second run (13/29 failures) was not verified directly. The origin codex thread consumed one real turn reacting to the workflow notification. The prototype patch is not scoped to the failing turn yet.

1860.title: Active steers ignore model/reasoning changes
1860.rootCauseOneLine: apps/app threadDetailPromptSubmission.ts buildSteerFollowUpRequest/buildFollowUpShortcutRequest (and EmbeddedThreadChat's steer) post {input, mode:"steer-if-active"} without the composer's model/reasoningLevel/permissionMode/serviceTier, so the server's buildExecutionOptions falls back to the active turn's last execution tuple and stores/dispatches the steer with it.
1860.proposedFix: Add an `execution: FollowUpExecutionSelection` argument to buildSteerFollowUpRequest/buildFollowUpShortcutRequest in apps/app/src/views/thread-detail/threadDetailPromptSubmission.ts and spread buildSharedThreadExecutionRequestFields(execution) into the steer-if-active request; pass followUpExecutionSelection from handleModifierSubmit in ThreadDetailPromptArea.tsx; spread executionRequestFields into the steer mutation in EmbeddedThreadChat.tsx handleModifierSubmit. No server/daemon/wire change needed (SendMessageRequest already accepts these fields; queued "Send now" and `bb thread tell --mode steer --model` already send them). Caveat: Claude Code applies model/reasoning live on steer; Codex's turn/steer cannot change the running turn's model, so for Codex the selection is recorded and takes effect on the next turn — consider disabling/annotating the picker while steering a Codex thread.
1860.caveats: Reproduced on Linux web dev app (headless Chromium, Playwright Meta+Enter) rather than the macOS desktop build; code path is identical. The dev-browser sandbox could not read request.postData(), so exact HTTP bodies were captured via a window.fetch hook inside the page (run 3). Codex provider semantics mean that even after the fix a mid-turn steer will not actually switch the model for Codex (only recorded / applied next turn); Claude Code does apply it live.
